subject: CloudGrid SLO measurement & remedies discussion
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: CloudGrid discovery — performance targets and open questions

Quick recap from today's discovery with CloudGrid (Samantha + Ops):

- Business ask: move their chat assistant from single-region infra to a multi-tenant hosted endpoint; must keep 95th pctl token-latency for streaming responses <= 300ms and p99 (non-stream) <= 450ms when concurrent sessions spike.
- Expected steady throughput: ~180 reqs/min with bursts to 750 reqs/min during office hours.
- Streaming requirement: partial tokens streamed as produced; user-facing latency critical for first-token (<120ms desirable).
- KV cache behavior: they will pin conversation context to keep seq lengths under 1024 tokens, but some inference paths will request 2.5k context via embeddings — we need to account for fallback model variants.

Open questions for legal/ops and for crafting SLA language:
1) How do we measure "latency" for streaming responses? (first-byte vs end-to-end completion)
2) What counts as an outage/exclusion: customer-caused network issues, malformed requests, heavy client-side CPU causing slow consumption?
3) Reporting cadence: quarterly SLO report + monthly high-level dashboards, but Ops asks for daily incident exports for 30 days after any breach.
4) Remedies: is a credit schedule acceptable (tiered by minutes of downtime or % SLO miss)?

Attachments from the call: I asked Samantha for their internal traffic profile (they'll share) — I attached the preliminary SLO draft we pulled together.

Next steps (internal):
- Karthik: draft suggested measurement language for streaming vs non-streaming, include definition for "first-token latency" and method to compute 95th for streaming.
- Grace: propose exclusion list and reporting cadence language that satisfies both legal and CloudGrid ops.
- I'll loop in customer success after we have a clean draft to send.

Thanks,
Ben

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: CloudGrid discovery — performance targets and open questions

Thanks for the clear recap, Ben — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our ops side that will help you draft the SLA wording:

- Latency: for streaming we care about "time-to-first-byte" (TTFB) and sustained per-token cadence. Our internal KPI is first-token <= 120ms (95th); end-to-end completion is less critical but should be < 1.5s for typical single-turn prompts.
- Measurement: we'll accept Redwood's server-side measurements (ingress timestamp vs first-server-transmit) provided that the method is documented and sampling is transparent.
- Exclusions: please explicitly exclude (a) customer network outages, (b) malformed payloads that cause server-side errors, and (c) maintenance windows that we agree in advance. We also want an explicit clause that heavy client-side slow consumption (i.e., the client not reading the stream) is an exclusion.
- Reporting cadence: monthly perf report + incident export on request for 60 days post-incident. Quarterly executive review is required as well.
- Remedies: CloudGrid prefers a tiered credit system. Example: 5-10% monthly credit for minor SLO miss (single-day breach), 10-30% for prolonged breaches. We can iterate on exact numbers with legal.

I've attached our internal network diagram for context. We'll share traffic-profile CSV by EOD Monday.

Samantha

samantha.lee@cloudgrid.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: CloudGrid discovery — performance targets and open questions

Good notes from Samantha — thanks. Draft approach I'm going to prepare for the customer-facing SLA:

- Definitions:
  * "First-token latency (FTL)": time from request ingest (server timestamp) to first byte transmitted to client.
  * "Completion latency": time from ingest to last token emitted.
  * Percentiles: SLO targets will be stated as 95th for FTL (<=120ms) and 99th for completion (<=450ms) for non-streaming endpoints.
- Measurement method: Redwood's server-side measurements will be source of truth. We'll include sampling method, measurement windows, and when we apply smoothing for short spikes.
- Exclusions: include the three Samantha listed + force-majeure and agreed maintenance windows.
- Reporting: monthly automated report + on-request incident export for 60 days; quarterly exec summary.
- Remedies: propose a tiered credit schedule (we'll draft percentages for legal to review).

Karthik: can you draft the streaming measurement text + a formula for computing 95th FTL across partial responses? Grace: can you draft an exclusions table and proposed reporting cadence text so I can reconcile into the SLO doc?

I'll aim to send a consolidated draft to Samantha by EOD Monday after K/G comments.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: CloudGrid discovery — performance targets and open questions

Ben / Grace — attached is a short draft for the streaming measurement section I put together. Key points:

- For streaming FTL we record per-request: ingest_ts, first_tx_ts, then FTL = first_tx_ts - ingest_ts. Compute 95th across a rolling 30-day window weighted by session.
- For sustained cadence we will include a per-token inter-arrival histogram (median and 95th) to surface stalls; this is considered a diagnostic metric and not part of the primary SLO but will be included in monthly exports.
- Sampling: to reduce cost we sample 20% of requests uniformly but ensure burst windows are fully captured for accurate tail estimation.

Redlines/questions: is 20% sampling acceptable to CloudGrid? If not, we can increase sampling during peak windows. Also propose adding an SLA appendix that defines measurement telemetry fields (ingest_ts, tx_ts, request_id) available in exports.

Karthik
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik — that approach sounds reasonable. A couple of follow-ups from legal/ops:

- Sampling: 20% is fine for the initial term provided you capture full-burst windows and we have access to raw exports on request.
- Appendix: yes, we want the telemetry fields documented for post-incident forensic work.
- Remedies: legal will propose exact percentages; we're generally OK with a tiered crediting approach.

Samantha
